name: Hiram Bingham to Machu Picchu
summary: A Yale lecturer looking for Vilcabamba, the last refuge of the Incas, follows the Urubamba gorge below Cusco. A local farmer, Melchor Arteaga, leads him up to Machu Picchu, where families still farmed the terraces; National Geographic's photographs of 1913 made it famous. He went on to find the real Vilcabamba at Espíritu Pampa without knowing it.

stops.note: The expedition sets out down the Urubamba.
Melchor Arteaga offers to show him ruins on the ridge above.
Two farming families are living among the terraces; a boy leads him to the temples.
The palace of Manco Inca and the sacred rock of Ñusta Hispana.
Overgrown ruins he dismisses; they were Vilcabamba itself.

informs.note: The Vilcabamba ranges surveyed; Machu Picchu photographed for the world
